lead: A triangular hillside neighbourhood, born of two large developments in the 1950s and one of the densest in Barcelona.
text: Verdun occupies former woodland that became farmland in the 19th century, mostly vineyards, in the west of the old municipality of Sant Andreu de Palomar. In 1904 the Carretera del Manicomi, today Carrer de Pi i Molist, and Passeig de Verdun were opened, and the first summer cottages of workers from the Sant Andreu factories appeared. In 1952 the Cases del Governador were built, 41 blocks to rehouse families from the Diagonal shanty towns on the occasion of the Eucharistic Congress. The Pla de Barris de Verdun allocates almost 5 million euros to some twenty projects through to 2028, including the redevelopment of Carrer de Casals i Cuberó and grants to renovate vulnerable buildings.

With 13,507 inhabitants in just 0.24 km², Verdun is the second most densely populated neighbourhood in the city, with 56,992 inhabitants/km². In the democratic era, community campaigns won the replacement of those blocks with new homes, with public spaces, facilities and services. It shares the Via Júlia with La Prosperitat, a rambla with shops and plenty of neighbourhood life, and at 2,736 €/m² and 759 €/month it offers moderate prices within the district. If you are selling, the average sale price is 7% below the Nou Barris average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 219,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Nou Barris (6th of 13 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 5% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of flats on hillside streets, very dense, and new homes that replaced the old Cases del Governador.
